Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the predictable pricing and rollout controls. Before we move procurement forward, two technical clarifications came up from our platform team:

1) Measurement windowing: do you report p50/p95 on rolling 1-minute windows, fixed 5-minute buckets, or something else? Our traffic has sharp bursts tied to end-of-minute batch jobs.

2) Regional differentiation: we need a clear commitment for the eu-west region with an explicit clause for scheduled maintenance windows and how exceptions are treated.

Can you point us to the doc that spells out what qualifies as an exception vs. a real SLO breach? If you can share a short proposal (1–2 pages) outlining measurement approach and an option for a limited exception policy, that would help us finalize the SOW.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Question on how you'd measure p50/p95 for high-variability routes

Hi Samantha — appreciate the clear questions. Short answers up front, followed by a sketched approach:

- Measurement baseline: Redwood reports both route-level and tenant-level p50/p95. By default we publish p50/p95 over rolling 5-minute windows for route-level alerts and rolling 1-hour aggregation for billing and SLA reporting.

- Why rolling 5m for route alerts: it balances noise from millisecond spikes while still surface-ing sustained degradation. Billing/SLA is coarse-grained (1h) to avoid transient blips affecting commercial outcomes.

- Exceptions and maintenance: we offer scheduled maintenance carve-outs (published 72h in advance) and emergency maintenance windows that require post-facto notification. Both are treated as excluded from SLA calculations if properly documented.

I attached a short proposal that lays out an alternative we sometimes offer for high-burst customers: response-tiering. Instead of a single global p95, we define traffic tiers (steady, bursty) per route and apply p50/p95 targets per tier with a simple aggregation rule for the commercial SLA. This reduces false positives for customers with spikey workloads.

Next steps I suggest: 1) you and your platform folks review the attached draft; 2) if agreeable, we convert the selected option into a narrow contract addendum (1 paragraph + measurement appendix). I can loop in Legal/Finance once you confirm the approach.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product — Redwood Inference
